lines.text: Pick any number. Round down the number, its double and its triple, then add them up.
lines.caption: Pick any number. Round down the number, its double and its triple, then add them up.

lines.text: Here's the surprise. No matter what you pick, you can NEVER get one thousand.
lines.caption: Here's the surprise. No matter what you pick, you can NEVER get one thousand.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out which numbers you CAN make.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out which numbers you CAN make.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: How many whole numbers n, from one to one thousand, can be written in this form?
lines.caption: How many whole numbers n, from one to one thousand, can be written in this form?

lines.text: n equals floor of x, plus floor of two x, plus floor of three x, for some real number x.
lines.caption: n equals floor of x, plus floor of two x, plus floor of three x, for some real number x.

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: First, what does floor mean? The floor of a number rounds it DOWN to a whole number.
lines.caption: First, what does floor mean? The floor of a number rounds it DOWN to a whole number.

lines.text: For example, the floor of seven over two is three. The floor of five is just five.
lines.caption: For example, the floor of seven over two is three. The floor of five is just five.

lines.text: So pick any x. Round down x, two x and three x, and add. Which totals can we make?
lines.caption: So pick any x. Round down x, two x and three x, and add. Which totals can we make?

lines.text: One quick note. A negative x gives a negative total, so we only need x of zero or more.
lines.caption: One quick note. A negative x gives a negative total, so we only need x of zero or more.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's draw a staircase graph, for x between zero and one.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's draw a staircase graph, for x between zero and one.

lines.text: Floor of x stays at zero the whole way. Floor of two x steps up to one at one over two.
lines.caption: Floor of x stays at zero the whole way. Floor of two x steps up to one at one over two.

lines.text: Floor of three x steps up at one over three, and again at two over three.
lines.caption: Floor of three x steps up at one over three, and again at two over three.

lines.text: Stack them up. The total climbs zero, one, two, three, one step at a time.
lines.caption: Stack them up. The total climbs zero, one, two, three, one step at a time.

lines.text: Each step is just one high, so nothing gets skipped. Yet!
lines.caption: Each step is just one high, so nothing gets skipped. Yet!

lines.text: Now watch x reach one. All three floors step up at the same moment!
lines.caption: Now watch x reach one. All three floors step up at the same moment!

lines.text: Floor of x becomes one, two x becomes two, three x becomes three. The total is six.
lines.caption: Floor of x becomes one, two x becomes two, three x becomes three. The total is six.

lines.text: So the total leaps from three straight to six. Four and five get skipped!
lines.caption: So the total leaps from three straight to six. Four and five get skipped!

lines.text: Add one to x, and the floors go up by one, two and three. That's six more.
lines.caption: Add one to x, and the floors go up by one, two and three. That's six more.

lines.text: So the pattern repeats every six: six, seven, eight, nine, then a leap to twelve.
lines.caption: So the pattern repeats every six: six, seven, eight, nine, then a leap to twelve.

lines.text: Divide by six. We can make remainders zero, one, two and three. Never four or five.
lines.caption: Divide by six. We can make remainders zero, one, two and three. Never four or five.

lines.text: Now count the skipped ones. One thousand is six times one hundred sixty-six, plus four.
lines.caption: Now count the skipped ones. One thousand is six times one hundred sixty-six, plus four.

lines.text: Each of those one hundred sixty-six blocks has one number with remainder four.
lines.caption: Each of those one hundred sixty-six blocks has one number with remainder four.

lines.text: One thousand has remainder four too! So that's one hundred sixty-seven.
lines.caption: One thousand has remainder four too! So that's one hundred sixty-seven.

lines.text: Each block also has one number with remainder five. That's one hundred sixty-six more.
lines.caption: Each block also has one number with remainder five. That's one hundred sixty-six more.

lines.text: Together, that's three hundred thirty-three numbers we can't make.
lines.caption: Together, that's three hundred thirty-three numbers we can't make.

lines.text: One thousand minus three hundred thirty-three is <short pause> six hundred sixty-seven! Choice A.
lines.caption: One thousand minus three hundred thirty-three is six hundred sixty-seven! Choice A.

lines.text: Here's another way. Count the numbers we CAN make, row by row.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Count the numbers we CAN make, row by row.

lines.text: Write the numbers in rows of six. Each row has four we can make, and two we can't.
lines.caption: Write the numbers in rows of six. Each row has four we can make, and two we can't.

lines.text: The full rows end at nine hundred ninety-six. That's one hundred sixty-six rows.
lines.caption: The full rows end at nine hundred ninety-six. That's one hundred sixty-six rows.

lines.text: One hundred sixty-six rows, times four each, gives six hundred sixty-four.
lines.caption: One hundred sixty-six rows, times four each, gives six hundred sixty-four.

lines.text: The last row is short: nine hundred ninety-seven up to one thousand.
lines.caption: The last row is short: nine hundred ninety-seven up to one thousand.

lines.text: The first three work. One thousand has remainder four, so it's out.
lines.caption: The first three work. One thousand has remainder four, so it's out.

lines.text: Six hundred sixty-four plus three is six hundred sixty-seven. Same answer!
lines.caption: Six hundred sixty-four plus three is six hundred sixty-seven. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this one? When the end of the list is tricky. You see it row by row.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? When the end of the list is tricky. You see it row by row.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: B, six hundred sixty-eight, is what you'd get if you forgot that one thousand is skipped too.
lines.caption: B, six hundred sixty-eight, is what you'd get if you forgot that one thousand is skipped too.

lines.text: C, six hundred seventy, is what you'd get if you stopped your blocks at nine hundred ninety and never checked nine hundred ninety-one to one thousand.
lines.caption: C, six hundred seventy, is what you'd get if you stopped your blocks at nine hundred ninety and never checked nine hundred ninety-one to one thousand.

lines.text: D, seven hundred fifty, is what you'd get if you thought one number in every four is skipped.
lines.caption: D, seven hundred fifty, is what you'd get if you thought one number in every four is skipped.

lines.text: Choice E is eight hundred thirty-four. That's what you'd get if you skipped only one number per block of six.
lines.caption: Choice E is eight hundred thirty-four. That's what you'd get if you skipped only one number per block of six.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Watch for big jumps, and check the very last number on its own.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Watch for big jumps, and check the very last number on its own.

scenes.chapter: Your turn: floor of four x

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same idea, with a small twist.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same idea, with a small twist.

lines.text: This time, add floor of x, plus floor of two x, plus floor of FOUR x.
lines.caption: This time, add floor of x, plus floor of two x, plus floor of FOUR x.

lines.text: How many whole numbers from one to one hundred can you make?
lines.caption: How many whole numbers from one to one hundred can you make?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

scenes.chapter: Floor of four x: the answer

lines.text: Draw the staircase from zero to one. At one over four, the total steps up to one.
lines.caption: Draw the staircase from zero to one. At one over four, the total steps up to one.

lines.text: At one over two, two floors step up at once. The total jumps from one to three. Two is skipped!
lines.caption: At one over two, two floors step up at once. The total jumps from one to three. Two is skipped!

lines.text: At three over four, it steps up to four. Then at one, it leaps to seven.
lines.caption: At three over four, it steps up to four. Then at one, it leaps to seven.

lines.text: One plus two plus four is seven, so it repeats every seven. Remainders zero, one, three and four work.
lines.caption: One plus two plus four is seven, so it repeats every seven. Remainders zero, one, three and four work.

lines.text: One hundred is seven times fourteen, plus two. Fourteen full rows of seven, with four in each row, give fifty-six.
lines.caption: One hundred is seven times fourteen, plus two. Fourteen full rows of seven, with four in each row, give fifty-six.

lines.text: Ninety-nine has remainder one, so it counts. One hundred has remainder two, so it doesn't.
lines.caption: Ninety-nine has remainder one, so it counts. One hundred has remainder two, so it doesn't.

lines.text: Fifty-six plus one is fifty-seven. That's the answer!
lines.caption: Fifty-six plus one is fifty-seven. That's the answer!

lines.text: The big idea: find where the floors jump. A jump bigger than one skips numbers.
lines.caption: The big idea: find where the floors jump. A jump bigger than one skips numbers.

lines.text: Here, the pattern repeats every six, and remainders four and five are always skipped.
lines.caption: Here, the pattern repeats every six, and remainders four and five are always skipped.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
